finding: SARS-CoV-2-infected mothers who underwent C-section had higher rates of comorbidities, pneumonia, and preterm birth, and experienced more hemorrhagic events, hypertensive disorders, thrombotic events, and ICU admissions compared to those who delivered vaginally.
mod_finding: C-section risk was associated with the presence of pneumonia, and 41.1% of C-sections in patients with pneumonia were preterm (Robson's 10th category).
